question: Does performance and method ordering persist when observations close to the declared MIC cutoffs are excluded?
prior_observation: Full stage6 model predictions and metrics have already been seen; this is not preregistered confirmation.
fixed: No fitting, thresholds, model, rules, phenotype cells or cohort representatives altered.
Original CCRE PHAS reference remains the primary CCRE reference.
Original EuSCAPE EUCAST14-derived reference remains fixed.
scenario: EUCAST14 Enterobacterales non-meningitis S<=2mg/L,R>8mg/L; I retained separately, never recoded to S/R.
analyses: Inventory raw MIC/source-category compatibility with the declared scenario; do not call disagreement a laboratory error.
Represent exact and censored source MICs as intervals without imputing a point.

Whole-source-MIC-interval and hypothetical one-twofold-dilution envelope [MIC/2,2*MIC]: define boundary-robust S/R only when every value in the envelope lies in the same declared S/R category. This is a stress assumption, not an estimate of measurement error.
Report all-case and boundary-robust and remaining strata for ML/broad/KPC and author CP controls, preserving original labels; no subgroup selection by outcomes.
Within each cohort retain original full-cohort selected cases and resampling groups; use10000 paired country draws(seed20261114) projected into each stratum, not newly selected representatives.
Report ML-minus-broad BA and source-composition percentiles, confusion counts and no superiority claim when tradeoffs/intervals disagree.
Independent interval logic and sklearn metric checks; all outputs including null/negative findings.
limits: No new independent temporal event or historical AST adjudication.
No inference that MIC uncertainty actually equals one dilution or that exclusions improve real clinical utility.
Stratification conditions on measured phenotype; core performance is not representative of all infections.
CCRE mixed assays are not newly remeasured BMD; EuSCAPE and CCRE share related surveillance origins.
